ranked_facts.why: Necrolytic migratory erythema is a characteristic skin lesion associated with glucagonoma, a type of pancreatic tumor, which is more likely to be related to metabolic/endocrine disorders (B1) or neoplastic disorders (B4), rather than inflammatory/autoimmune disorders (B2), infectious disorders (B3), or other conditions (B5).

Hyperglycemia is a common finding in metabolic/endocrine disorders (B1), neoplastic disorders (B4), and other conditions (B5), but it is less likely to be associated with inflammatory/autoimmune disorders (B2) or infectious disorders (B3).
